speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the rationale for maintaining the Silver Support (SS) Scheme's monthly income per person threshold at $1,500 for the higher tier benefit given that the Local Qualifying Salary has been set at $1,600; and (b) whether the Ministry will review the threshold for SS Scheme to ensure consistency and adequacy of support for lower-income seniors.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: I have two supplementary questions for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Given that Local Qualifying Salary (LQS), full-time equivalent as —

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I have not answered the Parliamentary Question yet.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I actually wanted to go on to the next question.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I am doing this because we have a lot of questions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, I want to confine and give priority to those who have filed questions, for the benefit of our Members.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
text: I understand that the LQS and the Silver Support Scheme are two different schemes.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
text: But given that there is a progressive increase from $1,400 to $1,600 since July 2024 for LQS, whether the Ministry has assessed how seniors whose wages were adjusted by employers to meet the LQS, have consequently been pushed into the lower Silver Support tier.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
text: This is mostly for those elderly who are staying alone in their own household.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
text: My second question is: how many Silver Support recipients have moved from the higher tier to a lower tier, since the LQS increase to $1,600?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But I think that perhaps he did not understand the construct of the LQS and the fact that it is not related to the Silver Support Scheme payout.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There will be further refinements to the LQS in the upcoming Budget, the Committee of Supply.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I do not think I want to go too much into the details.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Suffice to say, let me reiterate that they are not in any way interlinked.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I mean, that is not how we constructed the LQS to be.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Because the LQS, as I have shared earlier on, is aimed at working and solving our companies' needs for foreign workers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We do not want the companies to hire our locals on a token salary, so that they can get the foreign worker quota.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, please remember that they are not related.
